:::{#thm-quadratic-form-symmetric}
#### A quadratic form depends only on the symmetric part

If $\matr{S}$ is a $p \times p$ matrix and $\vx$ is a vector of length $p$, then

$$
\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx
=
\tp{\vx}\left(\frac{1}{2}(\matr{S}+\tp{\matr{S}})\right)\vx.
$$

So the value of a quadratic form depends only on the symmetric part
(@def-symmetric-part) of $\matr{S}$.

:::

::: proof

The quadratic form $\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx$ is a $1 \times 1$ matrix,
so it equals its own transpose:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx
&= \tp{\paren{\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx}}
&& \text{(a } 1 \times 1 \text{ matrix is symmetric)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,\tp{\matr{S}}\,\tp{\paren{\tp{\vx}}}
&& \text{(transpose of a product, twice)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\,\tp{\matr{S}}\,\vx
&& \text{(transposing twice changes nothing)}
\ea
$$

Averaging the two expressions for $\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx$:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx
&= \frac{1}{2}\paren{\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx + \tp{\vx}\,\tp{\matr{S}}\,\vx}
&& \text{(average of two equal numbers)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx}\paren{\matr{S} + \tp{\matr{S}}}\vx
&& \text{(distributive law)}
\\
&= \tp{\vx}\left(\frac{1}{2}(\matr{S}+\tp{\matr{S}})\right)\vx
&& \text{(move the scalar } \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ inside)}
\ea
$$

The distributive step is @thm-matmul-distrib,
and the transpose step is @thm-transpose-product.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-quadratic-form-symmetric}
#### Replacing a matrix by its symmetric part

With $\matr{S} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ from @exm-symmetric-part
and $\vx = (1, 1)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\tp{\vx}\matr{S}\vx
&= 1 + 2 + 0 + 3 \\
&= 6 \\
\tp{\vx}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\vx
&= 1 + 1 + 1 + 3 \\
&= 6
\end{aligned}
$$

Both quadratic forms equal the sum of their matrix's entries,
because every entry of $\vx$ is $1$.

:::
